THE front door. Re-engage an already-mapped target, or map a new one. Returns a PROJECT_MAP, the mounted workbench, and the next steps.

target.description: folder to attach to (default: the work target  -  the project this sidecar manages)

domain.description: force a cartridge (python-app | web-app | data-curation | records-research | generic) instead of detecting one; implies refresh

refresh.description: re-map even if a profile and map already exist

scope.description: narrow to ONE subsystem by name (e.g. 'frontend' or 'packages/web'): returns only that subsystem's workbench, policy, and pre-bound next. Nearest-ancestor resolution for composite targets.

project_map.description: domain + scores, shape, subsystems, entry points, vcs, signature, an optional model-written `synopsis` (purpose, when a summary backend is reachable), and an explicit `limits` list stating what the map does NOT know

workbench.description: mounted tool ids for this domain + per-tool policy (confidence + note)

staleness.description: reengage only: whether the target changed since it was mapped

next.description: ordered suggested calls  -  the workflow this front door points at

provenance.note: Walking skeleton of the front door (CHARTER.md sec 3 Layer 4). Structural only: no model, no embeddings. Writes solely into SUITE_HOME/workbench/.

tools.summary: Recovery ledger: make a multi-step effort durable and RESUMABLE across crashes. Start/advance/pause/resume with explicit failure classes; resume re-observes the target first and reports drift (stale_witness) rather than continuing onto a changed world.

action.description: start: open an operation. step: record a step outcome. pause: park with a witness. resume: re-observe then continue (or report stale_witness). finish/abandon: close. list/show: inspect (the recovery surface).

tool.description: step: the tool the step ran

args_hash.description: step: hash of the step's args (correlates to the event log)

failure_class.description: step: REQUIRED when status=failed. A generic failure is not allowed.

result_ref.description: step: pointer to the result (e.g. an evidence id)

idempotency_key.description: step: op-step identity; a resumed operation will not re-run a step with an existing key

resume_hint.description: pause: what to do next when resumed

resumed.description: resume: false when the target drifted

drift.description: resume: true = stale_witness, do not blindly continue

idempotent_hit.description: step: true = this step already landed, not re-applied

provenance.note: E4. Recovery as normal operation. A durable, resumable ledger ABOVE the event log (correlates raw calls into an operation - review sec 23), separate storage from journal/evidence (no truth-class collapse - review sec 9). Resume re-observes before trusting the paused world (review sec 13/17).

tools.summary: Surgical indentation-aware patching via JSON hunks (search/replace blocks); dry-run validate; preview by default.

The planner engine: turn an intention + a project map into a real, governed project. Runs genesis -> scaffold -> provenance -> journal as ONE resumable operation; preview-first, idempotent, and the built structure traces back to the intent.

action.description: propose: draft a map from intent (local model, degrades to archetype). preview: validate + show the whole plan, no writes. build: execute as a resumable operation (needs apply:true). resume: continue an interrupted build. status: show a build's operation.

intent.description: one sentence: what this project is for

map.description: the project map to build (from propose, or agent-authored). Required for preview/build/resume.

archetype.description: propose: bias toward a built-in archetype (python-cli | web-app | records-project)

root.description: destination directory for the new project (within the roots); default: <output_root>/scaffold/<name>

overwrite.description: build: replace files that already exist

apply.description: build/resume for real. Without it you get a no-write preview.

op_id.description: the resumable operation for this build

degraded.description: propose: true when no local model was usable (archetype returned)

trail.description: build: per-stage outcome (genesis/scaffold/provenance/journal), with skipped=true on resume

trace_hint.description: build: the provenance trace call to see why the project exists

provenance.note: E6. The planner ENGINE (engine before cockpit). Pure orchestration over genesis+scaffold+provenance+journal via the seam - adds no substrate, cannot become a monolith. First real consumer of the E4 operation ledger (resumable/idempotent) and E5 provenance (built structure traces to intent). The Tk cockpit (E7) drives this engine.

Formation provenance: record WHY an artifact exists (typed relations with an enforced origin - discovered | operational | interpretive), including multi-participant activities, and TRACE any artifact back to the chain that formed it.

action.description: note: one typed relation. activity: a multi-participant event. trace: walk backward from an artifact to its formation chain. list/show: inspect.

subject.description: note: the source entity {kind, ref, label}

relation.description: note: the relation (recommended: motivated, retrieved, supported, used, used_in, generated, derived_from, accepted_by, validated_by, superseded_by; any string allowed)

object.description: note: the target entity {kind, ref, label}

origin.description: REQUIRED on note/activity. discovered = found in the artifacts; operational = created by our work; interpretive = a model/heuristic guess, still provisional.

verb.description: activity: what the activity did (e.g. 'generate draft', 'move files')

participants.description: activity: [{role, kind, ref, label}] where role is e.g. requested_by | used | generated | approved_by | validated_by

op_id.description: the operation (E4) this relation/activity belongs to

ref.description: trace/show: the entity ref (path, id, url, text)

max_depth.description: trace: how far back to walk

chain.description: trace: the backward formation chain (subject -relation-> object, with origin)

origins.description: trace: which origin classes appear in the chain

provenance.note: E5. Records operationally-created relations (the gap for projects that BEGAN here) alongside discovered and interpretive ones, with the origin enforced. Higher-order activities keep multi-participant events coherent (review sec 23). trace answers 'why does this exist'. Separate truth class from journal/evidence/operations (review sec 9).

Resolved symbol graph: who actually defines and refers to whom (bound through imports, not name coincidence), plus CAS-cached one-line module summaries - with an honesty ledger of what static analysis cannot see.

action.description: stats: graph shape + honesty ledger. refs: a symbol's resolved callers/callees + its module's cached summary. build: persist the graph artifact. summarize: one-sentence purpose per module via a local model, cached by content hash (re-runs only touch changed files).

symbol.description: refs action: symbol to look up - a name ('start'), qualname ('Engine.start'), or id ('app.core.engine::start')

limit.description: refs action: max inbound/outbound edges returned per match

honesty.description: the unresolved ledger: dynamic dispatch, star imports, parse errors - the boundary of what 'no references' proves

summarized.description: summarize action: modules summarized this call (cached ones are free)

degraded.description: summarize action: true when no local model was reachable; missing modules are listed, never invented

provenance.note: D2/G6+G5. Replaces name-coincidence evidence with resolved edges; substrate shared with dead_code (two-tier reachability) and domain_boundary_audit (anchored relative imports) so all three answer from the same facts. Summaries ride the governed inference seam (llm_shared).
